I will still start from what worked for me before. On 60 mu, I will not spread myself too thin because some people in my house work off-farm, so I need the field work to be steady and manageable. I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the safest money here with well irrigation, and I will keep a smaller block in cotton for cash. Last year’s way is my base, then I adjust a little by cost and by what I saw on nearby fields that held yield. For wheat, I will feed it a bit heavier because if wheat is short and pale in spring, yield drops fast and I cannot easily get that back later. For maize, I will keep fertilizer solid but not wasteful, and I will use no-tillage after wheat on that land because summer work is rushed and labor is tight. Cotton needs more watching for insects and more water management, so I will not put too much area into it. Since I have a well, I will use irrigation to protect yield rather than gamble on rain. On big land like 60 mu, I care about efficiency too, so I will keep the rates simple and repeatable across plots.
